issue_context.title: `systemd-run --pipe` does not restore tty settings
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

254

### Used distribution

NixOS

### Linux kernel version used

6.5.7

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemd-run

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

Output of `stty -a` should be the same before and after running `systemd-run --pipe`

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

TTY settings changed by `systemd-run --pipe` and not restored.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Run a bash script:
```bash
stty -echo
stty -a
echo
systemd-run --user --pipe --wait --collect true
echo
stty -a
```

The output is below. Obviously `-echo` becomes `echo`.

(Original issue: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/262686#issuecomment-1775270043)

comments: hmm, systemd-run --pipe should actually not touch any tty settings at all

Interesting, different flags get changed when I try locally:

the changes are: `-imaxbel` -> `imaxbel`, `-echopr` -> `echoprt`

There is no change without `--pipe` arg.

systemd-254.5-2.1.x86_64
coreutils-9.4-2.1.x86_64
glibc-2.38-5.1.x86_64

Did some strace

`systemd-run` itself did not touch tty settings. But `systemd` (the service manager) made exact one `TCSETS` `ioctl` call.

It's like the `reset_terminal_fd` call in `setup_input` https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/d19434fbf81db04d03c8cffa87821f754a86635b/src/core/exec-invoke.c#L376-L400
